claims.statement: For each original leaf tag v, writing I(T-v,z)=I(H_v,z)+zI(R_v,z) and q_j=i_j(H_v)-i_j(R_v), the favorable selector is q_(p+1)-q_p+r_(p+1)-r_(p-1)<0 while the selected aggregate term is q_p-q_(p-1). The resulting coefficient-operator mismatch identifies the additional selector-aware global inequality needed by a generating-function route; the claw-free independence-polynomial real-rootedness theorem does not provide it for arbitrary trees.
claims.scope: Exact local decomposition for every original leaf of a finite ordinary tree; theorem-hypothesis audit for the lower-region target. This is a partial reformulation and obstruction to a blanket spectral argument, not a proof or refutation of either registered identity.
claims.reason: The decomposition follows directly by splitting independent sets of T-v according to whether they contain s_v. It exposes that selector and summand use different coefficient differences. The cited theorem requires claw-freeness and concerns individual independence polynomials; arbitrary target trees can contain claws and no selector-aware compatibility or global budget is established here.

limitations: No eligible ordinary-tree counterexample or proof of the lower-region aggregate was produced.
The real-rootedness theorem is inapplicable to arbitrary trees with induced claws, and even a claw-free special case leaves the selector-aware aggregate comparison unproved.
The exact global D+C budget in the supplied tagged-incidence identity remains open; no status is proposed for the auxiliary identity.
